topic: Sharing files safely: who can open your link
scope_note: Tool-neutral link-sharing practice for documents in cloud storage. No product names, menu wording, company policy, legal claims or statistics. Behaviour that differs between tools is marked varies by tool.

facts.statement: Cloud storage tools let you share a document by a link, and the link has a general access setting that decides who the link works for.
facts.reference_hint: Common to the help pages of major cloud storage vendors

facts.statement: With the broadest setting, anyone with the link can open the document, and in many tools they do not need to sign in.
facts.caveat: Names and sign-in rules vary by tool, and some organisations switch this setting off. Say: in many tools, and check your own.
facts.reference_hint: Vendor help pages on public or anyone links

facts.statement: With the company-wide setting, the link works for people who are signed in to your organisation's accounts, and not for people outside it.
facts.caveat: Exact wording and whether guest accounts count vary by tool and by company configuration.
facts.reference_hint: Vendor help pages on organisation-only links

facts.statement: With the named-people setting, the document opens only for the specific accounts you added, and each person has to sign in as that account.
facts.caveat: Some tools also allow a one-time code for people without accounts; this varies by tool.
facts.reference_hint: Vendor help pages on sharing with specific people

facts.statement: The three settings run from widest to narrowest: anyone with the link, then people in the company, then named people.
With view access, a holder can read the document but cannot change the original.
facts.reference_hint: Vendor help pages on viewer permission

facts.statement: With edit access, a holder can change the original document, and the changes are seen by everyone who uses it.
facts.reference_hint: Vendor help pages on editor permission

facts.statement: Many tools also offer a comment permission, which lets a holder add comments without changing the text itself.
facts.caveat: Not every tool offers comment access, and what it allows varies by tool.
facts.reference_hint: Vendor help pages on commenter permission

facts.statement: With view access, a person who can read the file may still be able to copy its content or download it, depending on the tool and its settings.
facts.caveat: Whether viewers can download, copy or print is a tool setting and varies; view protects the original, not the content from being copied.
facts.reference_hint: Vendor help pages on download and copy options

facts.statement: On the anyone-with-the-link and company-wide settings, the link itself is what grants access, so whoever holds it and meets the setting can open the document, however they got it.
facts.reference_hint: Vendor help pages and general guidance on link-based sharing

facts.statement: If a link on a broad setting is forwarded once, the new holder can open it without the sender being asked, and can forward it again.
facts.reference_hint: Follows from F10; company-wide forwarding still stays limited to signed-in company accounts

facts.statement: With named-people access, a forwarded link does not open the document for someone who is not on the list, because the tool checks the signed-in account.
facts.caveat: Applies where the tool enforces the list; behaviour varies by tool, and a listed person can still show or copy the content to others.
facts.reference_hint: Vendor help pages on restricted links

facts.statement: Before sharing, check you have the right file, choose the narrowest setting that works, and give view access unless the person needs to edit.
facts.reference_hint: Least-privilege principle in general security guidance, such as national cyber security agencies and vendor help pages

facts.statement: Before sharing, check who is on the access list, and check the file, including any other pages, comments and version history, for content that should not travel.
facts.caveat: Whether comments and version history are visible to viewers varies by tool; say check, not assume.
facts.reference_hint: Vendor help pages on sharing and on removing hidden data

facts.statement: Sharing a folder usually shares what is inside it, including files added later, so check the folder contents too.
facts.reference_hint: Vendor help pages on folder permissions

facts.statement: When access is no longer needed, switch the link off or change it to a narrower setting, and remove named people who no longer need the file.
facts.reference_hint: Vendor help pages on stopping sharing; least-privilege guidance

facts.statement: Reviewing your shared items from time to time helps you find old links still switched on, and many tools list what you have shared.
facts.caveat: How the list is found varies by tool.
facts.reference_hint: Vendor help pages on reviewing shared files; periodic access review in security guidance

facts.statement: Some tools let you set an expiry date on a link or on a person's access, so it ends by itself.
facts.caveat: Not every tool or plan offers expiry; varies by tool.
facts.reference_hint: Vendor help pages on link expiration

facts.statement: Your organisation may set its own rules or defaults for link sharing, so follow them where they differ from general practice.
facts.reference_hint: Organisations configure sharing policy in their admin settings

terms.definition: The general access choice that decides who a link works for.
Anyone who has the link in hand.
The permission a link or person gets: read only, or able to change the original.
Access limited to specific accounts you add.

not_claimed: Any statistic about how often shared links leak or cause breaches
Any breach story or named incident
That a link setting is technically unbreakable or that forwarding is hacking
That the company-wide setting is safe for anything sensitive without checking who is in the company
That view access stops people copying or downloading content
That a link with a long random address is a substitute for choosing the right setting
Any real product name, menu wording or default setting as universal
Any legal, compliance or company-policy requirement
